s: A company is assessing three applications before a data center exit in 18 months. App 1 is a commercial CRM whose on-premises version reaches end of support next year; the vendor offers an equivalent SaaS product. App 2 is a Java application on Apache Tomcat with a self-managed MySQL database; the team wants to stop patching and backing up the database but can change only configuration, not code. App 3 is a reporting tool that must stay close to an on-premises mainframe until the mainframe is modernized in 3 years. Which migration strategies should the company choose?
o: App 1: rehost. App 2: refactor into AWS Lambda functions with Amazon DynamoDB. App 3: retire.
App 1: repurchase. App 2: rehost both servers with AWS Application Migration Service. App 3: relocate.
App 1: replatform the CRM database to Amazon RDS. App 2: replatform to Amazon RDS for MySQL. App 3: rehost with AWS Application Migration Service.
App 1: repurchase. App 2: replatform by running Tomcat on Amazon EC2 and moving the database to Amazon RDS for MySQL. App 3: retain.

w.y: Moving to the vendor's SaaS product is repurchase, which also solves end of support. Moving the database to Amazon RDS for MySQL removes patching and backups with configuration-only changes, which is replatform. The reporting tool must stay close to the mainframe, so it is retained for now.

o.A: Rehosting keeps an unsupported CRM, refactoring needs code changes, and the reporting tool is still needed.
o.B: Rehosting keeps the self-managed database the team wants to stop operating, and the reporting tool must stay on premises.
o.C: The CRM still loses support, and moving the reporting tool away from the mainframe violates its constraint.
o.D: Correct: each strategy matches the stated constraint.

d: end of support; can change only configuration; must stay close to the mainframe
